description: Building an end-to-end Decision Support Copilot that bridges NASA Earth observation data (soil moisture, precipitation, and temperature anomalies) with actionable agricultural adaptation strategies using LLM-driven intelligence.
summary:
RotaSat is a free, interactive decision-support tool that helps farmers identify climate-resilient and economically viable crop rotations.
Users can select their field, explore soil and climate conditions, and compare crop rotation strategies based on profitability, soil health, water use, and climate resilience.

We use NASA POWER historical weather data and NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 climate projections to evaluate current conditions and future climate scenarios. Our system also simulates 1,000 possible future outcomes to help farmers understand the risks and potential benefits of different rotations.

RotaSat also uses NASA GIBS satellite layers (MODIS, SMAP), ESA Sentinel-2 imagery, and ISRIC SoilGrids soil data.
details:
What it does

RotaSat answers one question for a farmer: which crop rotation will still pay off on my field in 2050? The farmer taps their field on a satellite map, picks what they grow now, and sets what matters to them (profit, safety in bad years, soil health, saving water) and what limits them (water, machinery, market). RotaSat then tests 13 rotations on that exact field and shows the farmer's own rotation next to the best alternatives, for today's climate and for 2050.

How it works

For any field, RotaSat fetches 40 years of daily NASA POWER weather (1985 to 2024). A crop model based on FAO-56 Penman-Monteith and FAO-33 turns that weather into water stress, heat and frost damage and yields. Each rotation is run through 1,000 simulated futures of 20 seasons, built from real past years and real prices from 2000 to 2025, so the farmer sees the average profit and what happens in bad years. For 2050, the weather is shifted with NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 projections from five climate models and two emission paths. Soil carbon is tracked with the ICBM model, along with bare-soil months, erosion risk and nitrogen balance. NASA MODIS land cover checks that the tapped spot is really cropland, and NASA GIBS layers (MODIS, SMAP) show plant cover and soil moisture on the map.

Validation

We compared RotaSat's year-to-year results from weather alone with FAOSTAT national wheat yields from 1985 to 2023. In Germany it flagged all five worst harvests (r = 0.43); in Türkiye two of five (r = 0.41). Model choices were made on 1985 to 2004 only.

Benefits and impact

Farmers can test a change on their own field before risking a season. The tool makes the trade-off visible: a rotation that earns more may leave soil bare longer, and one that protects soil may need more water. It is free, needs no login, runs in any browser and works in English, Turkish and German, so it can reach small farms and advisers in both Germany and Türkiye.

Tools

HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single static page hosted on GitHub Pages, with Leaflet for maps, Chart.js for charts and SheetJS for Excel import. Data preparation scripts in Python.

Honest limits

The weather grid is about 50 km, the crop calendar is monthly, and pests and contracts are not modeled. RotaSat is a planning aid, not a forecast.

Use of AI

Code, design and text were written with help from Claude (Anthropic). This is stated on the site and in the README. No NASA endorsement is implied.
